title: Plannen maken met gaan
summary: The gaan-future: ik ga … doen, plus the time markers morgen, straks and volgende week

blocks.title: Ik ga … doen
blocks.body: The easiest way to talk about the future in Dutch: *gaan* + an infinitive. *gaan* takes the **V2** spot (second), and the other verb waits at the **end**. *Ik ga morgen werken* (I'm going to work tomorrow). It's exactly the English 'going to'.
blocks.callout: One verb rule: *gaan* second, the infinitive dead last.

blocks.title: gaan, helemaal
blocks.body: You already met *gaan* as 'to go'. Here are all its forms — same verb, now pointing at the future. Note *jij gaat* but in a question *ga jij* (the -t drops after inversion).

pairs.note: *straks* is still today: 'in a bit'. *later* is open-ended: 'when I'm older / at some point'.

blocks.prompt: Where does the second verb go? Pick the natural sentence.
blocks.explain: *gaan* is second, *doen* waits at the very end: *Ik ga morgen boodschappen doen* (I'm going to do groceries tomorrow).

blocks.prompt: Say 'I'm going to cook tonight.' (vanavond, koken)
blocks.hint: gaan second, koken at the end.
blocks.explain: *Ik ga vanavond koken.* Front *vanavond* and the verb still stays second: *Vanavond ga ik koken.*

blocks.title: Bouw een plan
blocks.prompt: Assemble a plan: who, when, and what you're going to do.

blocks.scene: Emma texts you about the weekend

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Wat ga jij dit weekend doen?
lines.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
lines.spotlight: ga jij … doen — infinitive parked at the end.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Ik ga zaterdag naar de markt en zondag ga ik luieren.
lines.en: I'm going to the market on Saturday and Sunday I'm going to laze around.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.target: Lekker! Zullen we morgen samen koffie drinken?
lines.en: Nice! Shall we have coffee together tomorrow?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Ja, gezellig. Straks stuur ik je een berichtje.
lines.en: Yes, fun. I'll send you a message in a bit.

questions.q: What is 'You' going to do on Sunday?

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the plan you hear.
Write three things you're going to do next week. Use *ik ga …* + an infinitive each time, and a different time marker.
